title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
slides: Cal AI went viral, but how?
Paid a small army of influencers to promote it.
The app didn't even work at first.
But influencers kept pushing it anyway.
If you're launching, test influencer marketing.
thread_text:
1. The AI App That Lied

Cal AI hit #1 on the App Store while its core feature didn't function. Influencers still posted tutorials praising it.

2. Army of Influencers

They paid hundreds of micro-creators to post before launch. Each video showed fake calorie scans that looked effortless.

3. Product Was Broken

The AI couldn't recognize food in early builds. Testers got error messages, yet sponsored posts rolled out on schedule.

4. Growth Before Truth

Downloads exploded because trust was borrowed from creators. By the time bugs were fixed, the hype had already done its job.

5. Test This Yourself

Pick one influencer and track if their promo matches reality. If they never show the app failing, ask why.
